 Bengaluru: The Income Tax Department has identified 11,458 high-risk cases across India, involving refund claims amounting to Rs 966 crore.
 ADVERTISEMENT This number is 1,441 in Karnataka and the amount involved is Rs 110 crore.
 The department has started issuing notices to those identified under high-risk refund cases, seeking explanations and demanding documents for refunds claimed.
 As explained by sources from the department, high-risk taxpayers are those who have filed returns seeking a refund by submitting what authorities suspect are fake certificates or documents.
 After verifying such cases, the department is also acting against employers of those identified as high-risk refund cases.
 Following the notices, some have started responding, requesting time to file updated returns.
 Also Read: APMC weighing inspection: Karnataka books 275 cases, levies Rs 9.8 lakh penalty In some cases, those identified accepted that their income-tax consultants had wrongly claimed allowances.
 The directorate of intelligence and criminal investigation of the department said 90% of these cases were reported in the salaried class.
 “In most cases, employees did not submit documents during the process of tax deducted at source by companies. But while filing returns, they submitted documents, of which a majority are fake,” explained a source.
 “For example, many have claimed lakhs of rupees as house rent allowance, but when we inquired with employers, the employees were found to have their own houses,” said the source.
 Now, with the identification of a massive number of such cases, the department is asking them to submit details of their returns claims of the previous three years.
 “This kind of tax evasion has become rampant in recent years. We are analysing data and before processing refunds, we are re-verifying in high-risk cases,” the source informed.
 As per documents available with DH , an employee of a private company claimed Rs 20 lakh in the last three years by submitting fake documents.
 Sources said the department can even recover money if the individual fails to rectify the same and update the income tax returns by paying additional tax.
 “Earlier, they used to claim deductions in the name of political donations. In December 2025, notices were served in that category. Now, submitting fake documents has become a trend,” the sources said.
